newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Heart specialist warns Yeltsin to take it easy.
newsitem.headline: Heart specialist warns Yeltsin to take it easy.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin's heart specialist has warned him to take it easy as he recovers from open heart surgery, Interfax news agency said on Wednesday.
It quoted Kremlin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais as saying the president was recovering well from the operation in November and was expected back in the Kremlin by the end of this month.
But Chubais told the agency that specialist Michael Debakey, a consultant in Yeltsin's treatment, had warned him not to take things too fast.

"The president received a letter from American cardiologist Michael Debakey, who wrote that he guarantees Yeltsin another 10 years of effective work on one condition -- that he always follows the schedule of gradual recovery and gradual return to work," Chubais said.
He said aides were preparing for Yeltsin's first full-scale meetings since his bypass operation on November 5.
"The health of the president of Russia is fine. I think that he will be back at work by the end of December. At least that's how things are planned now," Chubais said.
Some officials said earlier Yeltsin could return to the Kremlin next week, possibly on December 25 -- the fifth anniversary of his taking the reins of power from Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev.
The officials said Yeltsin was working on documents for several hours a day and taking long walks in the countryside around the exclusive Rus residence, where he is convalescing.

Chubais said Yeltsin's first foreign destination after his recovery would become known "in a couple of days". Aides have already said they expect a Russia-U.S. summit meeting, probably in the United States in March.
